speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have sudden-onset vertigo; to determine the cause, can you tell me if you experience any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ears during the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given the sudden onset of vertigo lasting only 3 minutes while lying down, followed by a return to baseline without hearing loss, this clinical picture is classic for BPPV. I will now request images of your inner ear canals to confirm the location of otoconia debris.

REQUEST IMAGES: Inner_Ear_Canals
